title: Comparison of Hyperparameter Optimization Methods and SHAP Interpretation of LightGBM for Medication Adherence Prediction in Non-Communicable Disease Patients: Code and Results
description:
Code, executed Jupyter notebook, data, figures and numerical results for a master's thesis in Informatics at Universitas Ahmad Dahlan, Indonesia (2026).

The study compares six hyperparameter optimization methods for LightGBM (Grid Search, Random Search, Halving Random Search, Optuna-TPE, Hyperopt-TPE and scikit-optimize-GP) using the Friedman test with the Nemenyi post hoc test. It explains the final model with four-level SHAP analysis and checks the robustness of the findings with a sensitivity analysis (class weighting, claim-unit feature ablation, and baseline vs final model with bootstrap confidence intervals and McNemar's test). Data: 24,084 insurance-claim records of diabetes and hypertension patients from Cimas Medical Aid Society, Zimbabwe.

Main findings: the highest mean 10-fold CV accuracy was 0.8241 (Random Search), with no significant difference between methods (Friedman p = 0.167). The final model reached accuracy 0.8201, MCC 0.6433 and AUC-ROC 0.9043 on the test set but did not differ from LightGBM's default configuration (McNemar p = 1.000). UNITSTOTAL had the largest SHAP contribution.
notes: Original thesis title (Indonesian): Perbandingan Metode Optimasi Hiperparameter dan Interpretasi SHAP pada LightGBM untuk Prediksi Kepatuhan Pengobatan Pasien Penyakit Tidak Menular.
